title: Concurrent fallback spike analysis and control plan
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Postmortem and mitigation plan for a multi-region concurrent fallback event that caused a spike in downstream load and SLO misses. This ticket captures timeline, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and tracked action items assigned to owners.
incident_summary: On 2026-03-04 22:43 UTC multiple primary region nodes entered a degraded state leading to simultaneous regional failovers. Fallback routing caused amplified fanout to secondary regions and a cascade of transient queue growth. Circuit breakers with narrow hysteresis repeatedly tripped and recovered, generating repeated warm cache misses. The net effect was a sustained p95 latency increase and a 28-minute SLO breach for hosted API customers across several tiers.
timeline: 2026-03-04 22:43 UTC: First alerts - elevated p95 and 5xx rate from primary-region-a (pager triggered)
2026-03-04 22:46 UTC: Autoscaler in primary-region-a reported rapid eviction events; partial GPU node pressure observed
2026-03-04 22:48 UTC: Traffic redirected to secondary-region-b via smart routing fallback policy; secondary-region-b's warmup hook executed
2026-03-04 22:49 UTC: Circuit breakers in secondary-region-b opened due to queue length thresholds; automatic fallback routed to tertiary-region-c
2026-03-04 22:50-23:08 UTC: Repeated trip/recover cycles across regions due to circuit hysteresis and cache coldstarts — observed 6 distinct fanout spikes
2026-03-04 23:09 UTC: On-call applied emergency policy to limit maximum cross-region fanout to 1.5x baseline (temporary throttle)
2026-03-04 23:22 UTC: Rolling manual adjustments to hysteresis windows and queue thresholds stabilized failover behavior
2026-03-05 00:05 UTC: Full mitigation verified; SLOs trending back to normal by 00:35 UTC
metrics: Duration of SLO miss window: 28 minutes
Concurrent fanout multiplier observed: 3.2x baseline during peaks
KV cache cold miss rate in secondary-region-b increased by 87% during warmup
root_cause: A compound failure: (1) simultaneous resource pressure in primary-region-a triggered fallback policy; (2) fallback routing allowed unconstrained concurrent fanout to healthy regions; (3) circuit-breaker hysteresis windows were too narrow leading to repeated open/close cycles; (4) KV cache warmup for fallback regions introduced higher per-request work which amplified queue growth; and (5) lack of a global fanout cap and insufficient early-warning runbook steps delayed automated mitigation.
detection_and_alerting: Existing alerts triggered on p95 and 5xx but were not correlated across regions. We lacked a cross-region aggregated signal for 'fanout amplification' and no SLO-derived alert with a short sliding window. The pager routed to the primary region SRE and did not surface the fanout pattern until post-aggregation metrics were available in Grafana.
mitigation_and_workaround: Emergency change: added temporary cross-region fanout cap (1.5x baseline) via control-plane override (change CL-1298)
Widened circuit-breaker hysteresis windows to reduce oscillation (PR #4142)
Enabled conservative KV cache prewarm for fallback regions (feature flag ff_prewarmpolicy=on)
Manual throttling rule applied for non-critical routes to preserve capacity for high-priority tenants
permanent_fixes: Add global fanout limiter in routing layer with configurable tiers and soft/hard caps (owner: Rafael Cruz, target: 2026-04-10)
Revise circuit-breaker default hysteresis to be workload-aware (owner: Anika Shah, target: 2026-03-28)
Implement cross-region aggregated alerting for fanout amplification and SLO drift (owner: SRE Team, target: 2026-03-22)
Improve KV cache pre-warming and warmup-to-capacity metric so fallbacks do not cause sudden work amplification (owner: Runtime Team, target: 2026-04-04)
Add a control-plane rollback-safe canary that simulates failovers in a low-risk staging region to validate routing policies (owner: Platform, target: 2026-05-01)
Update runbooks and playbooks to include explicit 'fanout amplification' steps and run automated diagnostic collection (owner: On-call Docs, target: 2026-03-18)
Introduce an automated circuit hysteresis tuning job that adapts based on recent trip/recover cycles (owner: Research/Applied ML, target: 2026-05-15)
